title: Neutrino Mass Ordering and the DESI Upper Bound
bottleneck: DESI plus CMB data cap the sum of neutrino masses at 0.072 eV, pressing against the minimum 0.059 eV required by the inverted ordering — potentially ruling it out cosmologically. But the bound relaxes if dark energy evolves, entangling neutrino physics with the DESI dark-energy hint, and laboratory ordering measurements (JUNO, DUNE) are still years away. If cosmology rules out the inverted ordering while long-baseline experiments confirm it, the contradiction would demand new physics such as decaying neutrinos.
why_it_blocks: Cosmology may determine the neutrino mass ordering before particle physics does, or the two may contradict each other, exposing new physics.
current_state: DESI DR2's extended analyses find the bound model-dependent; the ordering question is genuinely open on both fronts. The entanglement with dark energy dynamics means neutrino bounds cannot be read independently of the DESI evolving-dark-energy question.
